title: The homology-free boundary separates P from Q
body: The image descriptions alternately omit or impose freeness of $H_i$, whereas 063 explicitly defines $Q$ by freeness of $L_i,Z_i,B_i,H_i$. Over $\mathbb Z$, the complex $\mathbb Z\xrightarrow{2}\mathbb Z$ is bounded finite free, with free cycles and boundaries but torsion homology; it belongs to the category defined on 049 and cannot be a sum of the elementary acyclic complexes and free homology objects. This tests both 060's omission of $H_i$ in the claimed image of $P_1$ and 061's apparent imposition of free homology on all of $P$.

section: Universal complexes and relative exactness
title: A kernel can be admissible without its image inclusion being admissible
body: The warning “le mono $A'\longrightarrow B$ ne sera pas en général un $\Sigma$-mono” has a concrete explanation over a principal ideal domain: a degreewise image in a finite-free module is free, so the kernel sequence splits degreewise, but the subsequent inclusion can have torsion quotient. Already $2:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z$, placed in degree zero, has zero kernel and zero categorical cokernel in finite-free modules, yet is not invertible. This explains the deleted claim that the category is abelian and the surviving warning about bimorphisms.

section: Multiplicative structures and the de Rham comparison
title: A possible factorization proof using the source exact structure
body: Choose admissible injective presentations $X\hookrightarrow I^0\to I^1$ and $Y\hookrightarrow J^0\to J^1$, and suppose $X*Y$ is the admissible kernel of $I^0*J^0\to(I^1*J^0)\oplus(I^0*J^1)$ and $F$ preserves this kernel. Naturality of the product on injective objects makes the map $F(X)\otimes F(Y)\to F(I^0*J^0)$ vanish under both components, hence factor uniquely through $F(X*Y)$ using only biadditivity of the target tensor product at this step. Verifying that source-kernel presentation and its functoriality is the remaining task; this is not a proof of the whole extension theorem.
context: Context: this adds a conditional route to Hua, “L'unité, et l'extension aux foncteurs exacts à gauche”, and differs from a claim that preservation of kernels by $\otimes_B$ is already known to be necessary.

section: Multiplicative structures and the de Rham comparison
title: A minimal calculation separates cosimplicial and DGA commutativity
body: On the oriented edge $[01]$, take a zero-cochain $f$ with $f(0)=0,f(1)=1$ and a one-cochain $e$ with $e([01])=1$. The Alexander–Whitney product gives $(f\smile e)([01])=0$ but $(e\smile f)([01])=1$, although the pointwise function rings in every simplicial degree are commutative [BF04, §2.2.8]. This tests a distinction of products, not a claim that the interval admits no other commutative model.
context: Context: this adds an elementary illustration to the MPL_133 B06 lead and to Hua, “Le cup-produit”; it does not change the manuscript's own product formulas.
confidence: High: direct evaluation of the two endpoint formulas; standard example, with no novelty claim.

section: Multiplicative structures and the de Rham comparison
title: Good truncation is a plausible interpretation; naive truncation is not interchangeable
body: The phrase “complexe tronqué supérieur” and cohomology through degree $n$ fit a truncation ending in $Z^n(C)$, because the left-exact formula on 055 gives $F(\Psi^n)=Z^n(C)$. A naive truncation ending in all of $C^n$ generally changes $H^n$: the complex $k\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}k$ in degrees $n,n+1$ has zero $H^n$, while its naive upper truncation has $H^n=k$. This makes the exact truncation convention a substantive reading question, not harmless terminology.

section: Polynomial categories and divided powers
title: The two canonical maps need not be inverses
location: alpha construction; PD question and example
body: For $M=\mathbb Zx$ and $p,q\geq1$, write $e_n=\gamma_n^M(x)$ and $u_{p,q}=\gamma_p^{\Gamma^qM}(e_q)$: the representing map has $\alpha_{p,q}(e_{pq})=u_{p,q}$. Standard PD evaluation in the reverse direction sends $u_{p,q}$ to $\frac{(pq)!}{p!(q!)^p}e_{pq}$, so for $p=q=2$ its composite with $\alpha$ is $3\,\mathrm{id}$ [Stacks,07GL(5)]. The map $\alpha$ itself is an isomorphism in this rank-one case; the example shows that its inverse is not the standard PD evaluation.

section: Polynomial categories and divided powers
title: The PD operations require attention to degree zero
body: The usual divided powers on $\Gamma^*(M)$ are defined on its positive-degree augmentation ideal, so the reverse construction in P16 uses $q\geq1$. Requiring the usual PD axioms on the unit ideal of $\mathbb Z$, or on all of $\Gamma_{\mathbb Z}(M)$ would give $2\gamma_2(1)=1$, which is impossible. The abstract question should therefore specify its ideal and index range rather than conflate the degree-zero polynomial-category unit condition with PD operations on the unit.

title: The finite-set/Witt-vector bridge requires completion and a specified group
location: possible external comparison; not a construction named here
body: Dress–Siebeneicher identify the big Witt ring of $\mathbb Z$ with the completed Burnside ring of almost-finite sets acted on by the infinite cyclic group; finite cyclic sets give a proper dense subring [DS89, §1 and Theorem (5–4–2)]. In the profinite formulation, $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ gives big Witt vectors and $\mathbb Z_p$ the $p$-typical case [Mi14, introduction]. Witt groups of forms, for example the symmetric spaces modulo metabolic relations in [Ba05, Definition 1.1.27], are a different construction.

section: The binomial bridge, Witt and the planning questions
title: A Burnside ring need not itself be binomial
location: arithmetic degree warning; comparison with MPL_133 B01
body: Let $t$ denote the free orbit of $C_2$; orbit multiplication gives $A(C_2)=\mathbb Z[t]/(t^2-2t)$ with basis $1,t$ [L05, Definition 1.1, Example 1.4]. Then $\binom t2=t/2$ is not in $A(C_2)$, although cardinality sends $t$ to 2 in the binomial ring $\mathbb Z$. This prevents transferring binomiality from a numerical rank target to an arbitrary ring of finite group-sets.
context: Context: this adds an elementary test to the title of MPL_133 B01 and agrees with PS VI §120's distinction of operation structures, without claiming to identify the missing 133 rank map.

section: The binomial bridge, Witt and the planning questions
title: A divided-power algebra need not be binomial
location: module example and canonical PD structure
body: In the free divided-power algebra $\Gamma_{\mathbb Z}(\mathbb Zx)$, $x^2=2\gamma_2(x)$ but $\binom x2=\gamma_2(x)-x/2$ is not integral in the divided-power basis. Conversely, the binomial ring $\mathbb Z$ cannot have ordinary divided powers on its entire unit ideal, by the calculation in P17. These two tests show why a substantive construction is needed to connect the manuscript's PD structures with binomial cochains.
context: Context: this adds concrete distinctions to PS VI §120, pp. 506–507, and to the B01/B05 leads, while respecting the module example on 085.

section: The binomial bridge, Witt and the planning questions
title: A restricted filtered bridge can be proved directly
body: Filter $\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb Z)$ by polynomial degree: Newton expansion has integral coefficients $(\Delta^nf)(0)$, so the binomial polynomials $b_n(t)=\binom tn$ form a basis with $\deg b_n=n$. Leading terms give $\overline b_m\,\overline b_n=\binom{m+n}{m}\overline b_{m+n}$ and hence $\operatorname{gr}_{\deg}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb Z)\simeq\Gamma_{\mathbb Z}(\mathbb Zx)$ as ordinary commutative, weight-graded algebras. This is a precise rank-one bridge, with lower-degree terms deliberately discarded, not an equivalence of the homotopy theories in question.
context: Context: this adds a directly checked comparison to PS VI §119–120's binomial operations and to Hua's homogeneous $\Gamma^*$ framework; it does not settle WG2 §Week #3.

section: The binomial bridge, Witt and the planning questions
title: Constants show what the associated graded forgets
location: constant maps, degree-zero axioms, final enrichment
body: The polynomials $b=\binom t2$ and $c=b+t$ have the same degree-two symbol, but $b(1)=0$ and $c(1)=1$, so composition with a constant does not descend from these leading symbols alone. For positive-degree univariate polynomials, degree does multiply and leading composition is defined; specifically $\sigma_{mn}(b_m\circ b_n)=\frac{(mn)!}{m!(n!)^m}\overline b_{mn}$, matching PD iteration. A filtered lift must therefore reconstruct the discarded lower terms and check constants, units, substitution and eventually derived coherence, rather than rely only on R13.
context: Context: this adds a concrete obstruction to a too-quick bridge from Hua's homogeneous composition core to PS VI §120's analyzer operations, and makes the omission noticed on 083 relevant to the proposed comparison.
